questions.stem: Your team must keep a production app running even if one datacenter inside an Azure region fails, without leaving that region. Which feature should you use?

explanation.correct: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters within a single region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking, so losing one datacenter does not take the app down.

distractors.A: Region pairs span two different regions, not datacenters inside one region.
distractors.B: Management groups organize subscriptions for governance, not datacenter resilience.
distractors.C: Resource groups are logical containers for management and give no physical fault isolation.

explanation.exam_pattern: Survive a single-datacenter failure within one region = availability zones.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure regions, availability zones, and region pairs

questions.stem: A new teammate asks you to define an Azure region in fundamentals terms. Which description is correct?

options.text: A monthly invoice for Azure usage
A JSON template file that deploys resources
A geographical area containing one or more networked datacenters
A single server rack inside a datacenter

explanation.correct: An Azure region is a geographical area that contains one or more datacenters networked together with low-latency links.

distractors.A: That describes billing or an invoice, which is a subscription concept, not a region.
distractors.B: That describes an ARM template, not a region.
distractors.D: A rack is hardware inside a datacenter, far smaller than a region.

explanation.exam_pattern: Region = geographic area of one or more networked datacenters.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure regions, availability zones, and region pairs

questions.stem: Your team wants two Azure regions in the same geography where planned platform updates roll out to only one region at a time. Which concept describes this?

explanation.correct: Region pairs are two regions in the same geography; Azure staggers planned maintenance so updates reach only one region of the pair at a time, and the pair is also the target for geo-redundant replication.

distractors.A: Subnets segment a virtual network and are unrelated to regional update behavior.
distractors.B: Availability zones are separate datacenters within a single region, not a two-region relationship.
distractors.D: Availability sets protect VMs within one datacenter, not across regions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Two regions, same geography, staggered updates = region pairs.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure regions, availability zones, and region pairs

questions.stem: Which list shows the Azure resource management hierarchy ordered from the broadest scope to the narrowest?

options.text: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources
Resources, resource groups, management groups, subscriptions
Subscriptions, management groups, resources, resource groups
Resource groups, resources, subscriptions, management groups

explanation.correct: From broad to narrow, Azure organizes management groups, then subscriptions, then resource groups, then individual resources.

distractors.B: This is fully reversed; resources are the narrowest scope, not the broadest.
distractors.C: Management groups sit above subscriptions, not below them.
distractors.D: This inverts the hierarchy, placing resource groups above subscriptions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Broad to narrow: management group > subscription > resource group > resource.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: Your company has 20 subscriptions and wants to apply one governance policy to all of them at once. Which scope should you assign the policy to?

options.text: A management group that contains the subscriptions

explanation.correct: Management groups sit above subscriptions; a policy assigned to a management group is inherited by every subscription beneath it, covering all 20 at once.

distractors.B: Assigning per resource group is repetitive and would not uniformly cover whole subscriptions.
distractors.C: A single resource is the narrowest scope and cannot govern 20 subscriptions.
distractors.D: Availability zones are a resiliency feature, not a governance scope.

explanation.exam_pattern: Govern many subscriptions together = management group.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: A colleague asks what an Azure resource group is. Which statement describes it best?

options.text: A dedicated private network link into Azure
A logical container that holds related Azure resources for management

explanation.correct: A resource group is a logical container that holds related resources so they can be managed together, such as deployed, updated, or deleted as a unit.

distractors.A: A datacenter is a physical facility, not a logical container.
distractors.B: That describes ExpressRoute, a connectivity service, not a resource group.
distractors.C: That describes billing through a subscription or account, not a resource group.

explanation.exam_pattern: Resource group = logical container for related resources.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: A developer deletes a resource group that holds a VM, its disk, and a storage account. What happens to those resources?

options.text: Only the group name is removed; the resources remain
The resources move to a default group automatically
Only the VM is deleted; the disk and storage remain
All resources in the group are deleted

explanation.correct: Resources share the lifecycle of their resource group, so deleting the group deletes every resource contained in it.

distractors.A: Deleting a group is not just a rename; its contents are removed as well.
distractors.B: Resources are not auto-migrated on deletion; they are removed with the group.
distractors.C: Deletion is not selective; all contained resources go, not only the VM.

explanation.exam_pattern: Delete the resource group and you delete everything inside it.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: You need to know how many resource groups a single resource, such as one virtual machine, can belong to at the same time. What is correct?

explanation.correct: Each Azure resource belongs to exactly one resource group at a time, though it can be moved to a different group later.

distractors.A: A resource cannot belong to two resource groups simultaneously.
distractors.B: Membership is not unlimited; it is exactly one group at a time.
distractors.D: Every resource must reside in a resource group, so zero is incorrect.

explanation.exam_pattern: One resource lives in exactly one resource group at a time.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: Every request to create, update, or delete Azure resources from the portal, CLI, PowerShell, or templates is processed by which service?

explanation.correct: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is the unified deployment and management layer that handles all resource create, update, and delete requests, no matter which tool issues them.

distractors.A: Azure Monitor collects telemetry and metrics; it does not process resource requests.
distractors.C: Microsoft Entra ID handles identity and access, not resource deployment.
distractors.D: Blob Storage stores data objects and is not the management layer.

explanation.exam_pattern: All resource management requests flow through Azure Resource Manager.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure Resource Manager (ARM)

questions.stem: Your finance team wants completely separate invoices for the development and production workloads. Which Azure boundary most directly separates billing?

options.text: Separate resource groups in one subscription

explanation.correct: A subscription is a billing and access boundary, so placing dev and prod in separate subscriptions produces separate invoices.

distractors.A: Resource groups organize resources but do not generate separate invoices by themselves.
distractors.C: Availability zones are a resiliency feature, unrelated to billing separation.
distractors.D: Tags help categorize and report costs but do not split billing into separate invoices.

explanation.exam_pattern: Separate invoices = separate subscriptions.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups

questions.stem: A regulator requires that your customer data stay within a specific country's boundaries. Which Azure concept is defined to preserve data residency and compliance?

explanation.correct: A geography is a discrete market, often aligned to country or compliance boundaries, that ensures data residency; region pairs always stay within the same geography.

distractors.B: An availability zone is a datacenter grouping inside one region, not a data-residency boundary.
distractors.C: A resource group is a logical management container, not a compliance or residency boundary.
distractors.D: A subnet segments a virtual network and has nothing to do with data residency.

explanation.exam_pattern: Data-residency and compliance boundary = geography.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions

questions.stem: A developer must run a small piece of code only when a queue message arrives, and pay only while it runs. Which service fits best?

explanation.correct: Azure Functions is serverless and event-driven: code runs in response to a trigger such as a queue message, you pay only for the execution, and it scales automatically.

distractors.B: App Service hosts always-running web apps, not pay-per-execution event code.
distractors.C: A VM runs continuously and must be managed and paid for even when idle.
distractors.D: AKS orchestrates containers and adds management overhead unnecessary for a tiny function.

explanation.exam_pattern: Event-triggered, pay-per-run code = Azure Functions (serverless).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: Your company needs a private, dedicated connection to Azure that does not travel over the public internet, with predictable low latency. Which service meets this?

explanation.correct: ExpressRoute provides a private, dedicated connection to Azure through a connectivity provider, bypassing the public internet for more consistent latency and bandwidth.

distractors.A: A public endpoint is reached over the internet, the opposite of a private dedicated link.
distractors.C: Azure DNS resolves domain names and is not a connectivity circuit.
distractors.D: A VPN Gateway is encrypted but still carries traffic across the public internet.

explanation.exam_pattern: Private, dedicated, off-the-internet link = ExpressRoute.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure networking (virtual networks, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS)

questions.stem: A small branch office needs an encrypted site-to-site tunnel to Azure over its existing internet connection, with no dedicated circuit. Which service fits?

explanation.correct: A VPN Gateway creates encrypted IPsec/IKE tunnels to Azure over the public internet, so a branch can connect without provisioning a dedicated circuit.

distractors.B: Azure Functions runs code and is unrelated to network connectivity.
distractors.C: ExpressRoute requires a provider-provisioned private circuit, which the scenario rules out.
distractors.D: An availability set spreads VMs for resiliency and does not connect networks.

explanation.exam_pattern: Encrypted tunnel over the public internet = VPN Gateway.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure networking (virtual networks, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS)

questions.stem: You want to protect several VMs from a hardware fault or planned maintenance within a single datacenter. Which feature spreads them across fault and update domains?

explanation.correct: An availability set distributes VMs across fault domains and update domains inside one datacenter, protecting them from localized hardware failures and planned maintenance.

distractors.B: A scale set manages identical VMs for scaling; it is not the fault/update-domain resiliency construct.
distractors.C: A resource group is a logical container and provides no physical fault isolation.
distractors.D: Availability zones protect across separate datacenters in a region, not within one datacenter's domains.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fault and update domains within one datacenter = availability set.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: Your web tier must automatically add or remove identical, load-balanced VMs as traffic rises and falls. Which capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Virtual machine scale sets create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs and automatically scale their number based on demand or a schedule.

distractors.A: Availability sets improve resiliency but do not autoscale the number of VMs.
distractors.B: ExpressRoute is a connectivity service, unrelated to autoscaling VMs.
distractors.D: Azure Container Instances runs containers, not a managed fleet of VMs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Autoscaling a fleet of identical VMs = scale sets.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: Your team is deploying dozens of microservice containers that need orchestration, scaling, and self-healing. Which service is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is managed Kubernetes for orchestrating many containers at scale, including scheduling, scaling, and self-healing.

distractors.A: Azure Container Instances runs single or simple containers without an orchestrator.
distractors.C: Azure DNS resolves names and is unrelated to running containers.
distractors.D: Azure Functions runs event-driven code, not container orchestration.

explanation.exam_pattern: Orchestrate many containers at scale = AKS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: A developer wants the fastest, simplest way to run a single container in Azure without managing servers or an orchestrator. Which service should they choose?

explanation.correct: Azure Container Instances (ACI) is the quickest, simplest way to run a container serverlessly, with no VM or orchestrator to manage.

distractors.B: ExpressRoute is a networking service and cannot run containers.
distractors.C: AKS adds orchestration and cluster management overhead not needed for a single container.
distractors.D: A VM requires you to manage the operating system and container runtime yourself.

explanation.exam_pattern: One container, no orchestration, fastest start = ACI.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: Your team wants to host a scalable web app and REST API without managing the underlying operating system or servers. Which service fits best?

explanation.correct: Azure App Service is a platform-as-a-service offering that hosts web apps and APIs with built-in scaling and no operating system for you to manage.

distractors.A: An availability zone is a resiliency construct, not an app-hosting service.
distractors.C: A VM is infrastructure-as-a-service, so you must manage and patch the OS yourself.
distractors.D: Azure Data Box is a data-transfer appliance, not a web host.

explanation.exam_pattern: Managed web/API hosting with no OS to manage = App Service (PaaS).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: You must divide a virtual network's private address space into smaller ranges for different tiers of an application. What do you create?

explanation.correct: Subnets segment a virtual network's address space into smaller ranges so you can separate and control the tiers of an application.

distractors.A: Resource groups are management containers, not network segments.
distractors.B: Storage accounts hold data and are unrelated to network segmentation.
distractors.C: Management groups organize subscriptions, not IP address ranges.

explanation.exam_pattern: Segment a virtual network's address space = subnets.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure networking (virtual networks, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS)

questions.stem: You want to reach an Azure storage account from your virtual network using a private IP address so traffic never crosses the public internet. What should you configure?

options.text: An Azure DNS zone by itself
A VPN Gateway to the storage account

explanation.correct: A private endpoint uses Azure Private Link to give the service a private IP inside your virtual network, keeping traffic off the public internet.

distractors.A: A public endpoint is internet-facing, the opposite of what is required.
distractors.B: A DNS zone resolves names but does not by itself move traffic onto a private path.
distractors.C: A VPN Gateway connects whole networks; it does not attach a private IP to an individual PaaS service.

explanation.exam_pattern: Private IP to a PaaS service, off the internet = private endpoint (Private Link).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure networking (virtual networks, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS)

questions.stem: Your team wants to host your domain's DNS records in Azure and resolve names using Microsoft's global name servers. Which service provides this?

explanation.correct: Azure DNS hosts your DNS domains and records and resolves names using Microsoft's global DNS infrastructure.

distractors.A: Azure Functions runs code and does not host DNS zones.
distractors.B: An availability set is a VM resiliency feature, unrelated to DNS.
distractors.D: A VPN Gateway provides encrypted connectivity, not DNS hosting.

explanation.exam_pattern: Host DNS records in Azure = Azure DNS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure networking (virtual networks, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS)

questions.stem: Your architect wants compute options where Azure manages the operating system for you. Which TWO of the following are platform-as-a-service (PaaS) options? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Azure App Service and Azure Functions are platform/serverless (PaaS) services: Azure manages the underlying operating system and infrastructure, and you supply only your app or code.

distractors.A: Virtual machine scale sets are groups of VMs, so you still manage their operating system (IaaS).
distractors.C: Azure Virtual Machines is infrastructure-as-a-service; you manage the guest operating system.

explanation.exam_pattern: App Service and Functions = PaaS (no OS to manage); VMs and scale sets = IaaS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure compute services (VMs, containers, Azure Functions, App Service)

questions.stem: Your application must store millions of images and video files as objects with massive scalability. Which Azure Storage service is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Blob storage is Azure's object store for unstructured data such as images, video, documents, and backups, and it scales massively.

distractors.A: Disk storage provides block volumes attached to VMs, not an object store.
distractors.C: Table storage is a NoSQL key-value store, not an object store for media files.
distractors.D: Queue storage holds messages for component communication, not large media objects.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unstructured objects (images, video, backups) = Blob storage.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: You need a fully managed file share that multiple VMs and on-premises machines can mount over SMB. Which storage option fits?

explanation.correct: Azure Files provides fully managed file shares accessible over SMB (and NFS) that cloud and on-premises machines can mount concurrently.

distractors.B: Queue storage holds messages, not files.
distractors.C: A managed disk attaches to a single VM and is not a shared file share.
distractors.D: Blob storage serves objects through HTTP APIs, not a mountable SMB file share.

explanation.exam_pattern: Managed SMB file share mountable by many clients = Azure Files.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: An Azure VM needs a block-level storage volume that behaves like a physical hard drive attached to it. Which storage type is this?

explanation.correct: Managed disks are block-level storage volumes attached to Azure VMs, functioning like a hard drive for the VM.

distractors.B: A blob container stores objects, not a block volume for a VM's operating system or data disk.
distractors.C: Queue storage holds messages and is not block storage.
distractors.D: An Azure Files share is a network file share, not a VM block disk.

explanation.exam_pattern: Block volume attached to a VM = managed disk.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: Two parts of your application must exchange large numbers of messages asynchronously so they can scale independently. Which storage service suits this?

explanation.correct: Queue storage stores large numbers of messages, letting application components communicate asynchronously and scale independently.

distractors.A: Azure Files provides file shares, not asynchronous messaging.
distractors.C: Disk storage provides VM volumes, not a messaging queue.
distractors.D: Blob storage holds objects, not a message queue for decoupling components.

explanation.exam_pattern: Async messages between components = Queue storage.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: Which redundancy option keeps three copies of your data within a single datacenter in the primary region at the lowest cost?

explanation.correct: LRS replicates data three times within a single datacenter in the primary region; it is the lowest-cost option but does not survive a datacenter outage.

distractors.B: GRS also replicates to a second region, so it is not confined to one datacenter.
distractors.C: ZRS copies data across availability zones, not within a single datacenter.
distractors.D: GZRS combines zone and geo redundancy and is not confined to a single datacenter.

explanation.exam_pattern: Three copies in one datacenter, cheapest = LRS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: You must keep storage available even if an entire datacenter in the region fails, while keeping all copies within that one region. Which option fits?

explanation.correct: ZRS replicates data synchronously across three availability zones within the primary region, so it survives a single datacenter (zone) failure while staying in-region.

distractors.B: GRS copies data to a second region, which goes beyond the in-region requirement.
distractors.C: LRS keeps all copies in one datacenter, so a datacenter failure could lose access.
distractors.D: RA-GRS also replicates to a second region, so copies leave the single region.

explanation.exam_pattern: Survive a datacenter loss while staying in one region = ZRS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: Your compliance policy requires storage data to survive a complete regional outage by replicating to Azure's paired region. Which redundancy option provides this?

explanation.correct: GRS replicates data to the paired secondary region in addition to the primary, so it survives a complete regional outage.

distractors.A: The hot tier is an access-frequency setting, not a redundancy option at all.
distractors.C: LRS stays in one datacenter and cannot survive a regional outage.
distractors.D: ZRS stays within the primary region, so a full regional outage could still affect it.

explanation.exam_pattern: Survive a whole-region outage via the paired region = GRS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: You want the highest durability: zone redundancy within the primary region plus replication to the paired region. Which option combines both?

explanation.correct: GZRS writes data across availability zones in the primary region (like ZRS) and also replicates to the paired secondary region, combining zone and geo protection.

distractors.B: GRS replicates to a second region but keeps the primary copy as LRS, not zone-redundant.
distractors.C: ZRS protects across zones but does not replicate to a second region.
distractors.D: LRS is single-datacenter, offering neither zone nor geo redundancy.

explanation.exam_pattern: Zone redundancy plus geo replication = GZRS.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage services and redundancy

questions.stem: You must retain compliance backups that are almost never read, at the lowest storage cost, and can tolerate hours of retrieval latency. Which blob access tier fits?

explanation.correct: The archive tier offers the lowest storage cost for rarely accessed data, but it is offline, so data must be rehydrated (which can take hours) before it can be read.

distractors.A: The cold tier stores rarely accessed data online, without archive's lowest cost or hours-long rehydration.
distractors.B: The cool tier is for infrequently accessed data that still stays online and readily available.
distractors.D: The hot tier is optimized for frequent access with the highest storage cost.

explanation.exam_pattern: Rarely read, cheapest storage, retrieval delay acceptable = archive tier.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage access tiers

questions.stem: A dataset is read many times every day and must return immediately. Which blob access tier minimizes access (read) costs for this pattern?

explanation.correct: The hot tier has the highest storage cost but the lowest access cost and immediate availability, making it ideal for frequently read data.

distractors.A: The cold tier targets rarely accessed data and has higher access costs than hot.
distractors.C: The cool tier lowers storage cost but raises access cost, so frequent reads become expensive.
distractors.D: The archive tier is offline and requires rehydration, so it cannot return data immediately.

explanation.exam_pattern: Frequent reads with instant access = hot tier.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure storage access tiers

questions.stem: You must move 80 TB into Azure, but your internet link is too slow to transfer it in reasonable time. Which option fits?

explanation.correct: Azure Data Box is a physical appliance Microsoft ships to you so you can load data locally and return it, ideal for large offline transfers when the network is impractical.

distractors.A: AzCopy transfers over the network, which the scenario says is too slow for this volume.
distractors.B: A private endpoint controls a network access path, not bulk offline migration.
distractors.D: Azure DNS resolves names and has nothing to do with bulk data transfer.

explanation.exam_pattern: Huge offline transfer when the network is too slow = Data Box.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure data migration options (Azure Migrate, Azure Data Box, AzCopy)

questions.stem: An administrator wants a command-line tool to copy blobs and files to and from Azure Storage over the network with scriptable commands. Which tool fits?

explanation.correct: AzCopy is a command-line utility for copying data to and from Blob and Azure Files storage over the network, well suited to scripted transfers.

distractors.A: Azure Monitor collects telemetry and does not copy storage data.
distractors.B: Azure Data Box is a physical appliance for offline transfer, not a command-line tool.
distractors.D: Azure Migrate discovers and migrates servers and workloads, not simple scripted file copies.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scriptable command-line copy to/from storage = AzCopy.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure data migration options (Azure Migrate, Azure Data Box, AzCopy)

questions.stem: Before moving to Azure, your team wants to discover on-premises servers, assess their readiness, and then migrate them. Which service is the central hub for this?

explanation.correct: Azure Migrate is a central hub to discover, assess, and migrate on-premises servers, databases, and other workloads to Azure.

distractors.A: Azure DNS resolves names and is unrelated to migration assessment.
distractors.B: AzCopy only copies storage data; it does not assess or migrate servers.
distractors.C: Azure Files provides file shares, not a migration assessment and move service.

explanation.exam_pattern: Discover, assess, and migrate servers to Azure = Azure Migrate.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Azure data migration options (Azure Migrate, Azure Data Box, AzCopy)

questions.stem: Which Azure service provides cloud-based identity and access management for users signing in to applications, and was formerly called Azure Active Directory?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Azure's cloud identity and access management service for users, groups, and application sign-in.

distractors.A: Blob Storage stores data objects and does not manage identities.
distractors.B: Azure Resource Manager deploys and manages resources; it is not an identity service.
distractors.C: A virtual network provides networking, not identity services.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cloud identity and access management = Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Microsoft Entra ID

questions.stem: When a user signs in and the system verifies their identity by checking their credentials, which process is taking place?

explanation.correct: Authentication is the process of verifying who a user is, typically by checking credentials such as a password.

distractors.B: Encryption protects data confidentiality; it is not identity verification.
distractors.C: Authorization determines what an already-identified user may do, which is a later step.
distractors.D: Load balancing distributes network traffic and is unrelated to verifying identity.

explanation.exam_pattern: Proving who you are = authentication.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe authentication and authorization

questions.stem: After a user has signed in, Azure checks whether they are permitted to delete a particular resource. Which process does this permission check represent?

explanation.correct: Authorization determines what an authenticated user is allowed to do, such as whether they may delete a resource.

distractors.A: Authentication verifies identity and happens before the permission check.
distractors.B: Multi-factor authentication strengthens sign-in, not what actions are permitted.
distractors.D: Single sign-on reduces repeated sign-ins; it does not decide permissions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Deciding what you are allowed to do = authorization.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe authentication and authorization

questions.stem: Your employees want to sign in once and then open many different applications without re-entering their password each time. Which capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Single sign-on (SSO) lets a user authenticate once and then access multiple applications without signing in again for each one.

distractors.A: ExpressRoute is a connectivity service and has nothing to do with sign-in.
distractors.B: Multi-factor authentication adds verification steps, increasing prompts rather than reducing them.
distractors.C: Locally redundant storage is a data-redundancy option, unrelated to sign-in.

explanation.exam_pattern: Sign in once, reach many apps = single sign-on.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe authentication and authorization

questions.stem: To harden sign-ins, you require users to provide both a password and a one-time code from their phone. What is this practice called?

explanation.correct: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) requires two or more independent verification factors, such as a password plus a phone code, strengthening sign-in security.

distractors.B: Conditional Access is a policy engine that can require MFA, but the act of providing two factors is MFA itself.
distractors.C: Single sign-on reduces repeated sign-ins; it does not add verification factors.
distractors.D: Authorization governs permissions after sign-in, not the number of sign-in factors.

explanation.exam_pattern: Two or more verification factors = multi-factor authentication.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe authentication and authorization

questions.stem: You want to block sign-ins from outside your country and require extra verification when access comes from an unmanaged device. Which Entra ID feature enforces such if-then rules?

explanation.correct: Conditional Access applies if-then policies that use signals such as location, device state, and risk to allow, block, or add requirements like MFA.

distractors.B: Azure DNS resolves names and does not enforce access policy.
distractors.C: Single sign-on streamlines sign-in but does not evaluate access conditions.
distractors.D: Availability zones are a resiliency feature, unrelated to access policies.

explanation.exam_pattern: Signal-based if-then access rules = Conditional Access.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Conditional Access

questions.stem: Your company must let partner-organization users access a shared app using their own existing credentials as guests. Which capability supports this?

options.text: Microsoft Entra External ID business-to-business (B2B) collaboration

explanation.correct: B2B collaboration, part of Microsoft Entra External ID, invites external partners as guest users who sign in with their own organization's credentials.

distractors.A: Locally redundant storage is a data-redundancy option, not an identity feature.
distractors.B: B2C is for consumer/customer identities on customer-facing apps, not partner guest access.

questions.stem: You are building a public shopping app where millions of customers create their own accounts or sign in with social logins. Which identity solution is designed for this?

distractors.A: Azure Files is a storage service and does not manage customer identities.
distractors.B: On-premises Active Directory Domain Services manages internal corporate identities, not public customer accounts.
distractors.C: B2B collaboration is for partner organizations, not millions of consumer customers.

explanation.exam_pattern: Consumer-facing sign-up/sign-in with social logins = Entra External ID B2C.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Microsoft Entra External ID

questions.stem: A colleague assumes Microsoft Entra ID is simply on-premises Active Directory running in the cloud. Which statement correctly distinguishes them?

options.text: On-premises AD is a cloud-only service that has no domain controllers
Entra ID is a cloud identity service using internet protocols such as HTTP/HTTPS; it is not a lifted-and-shifted on-premises AD domain controller
Entra ID uses organizational units and Group Policy exactly like on-premises AD
Entra ID and on-premises AD are identical in features and structure

explanation.correct: Entra ID is cloud-based and uses internet protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) for web and cloud app identity; it is not the same as on-premises AD Domain Services, which uses protocols like LDAP and Kerberos with domain controllers.

distractors.C: Organizational units and Group Policy are on-premises AD DS features, not how Entra ID works.
distractors.D: They differ in structure and capabilities; they are not identical.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Microsoft Entra ID

questions.stem: A teammate suggests using Microsoft Entra ID to store the company's large video files. Why is that the wrong tool?

options.text: Entra ID is an identity and access service, not a data store; large files belong in Blob storage
Entra ID stores files but cannot authenticate users
Entra ID can store files, but only those under 1 GB
Entra ID stores files only in the archive access tier

distractors.B: Authenticating users is exactly what Entra ID does; the false claim is that it stores files.
distractors.C: Entra ID is not a file store at all, so a size limit for stored files does not apply.
distractors.D: Access tiers are a Blob storage concept, not an Entra ID capability.

explanation.exam_pattern: Entra ID = identity, not a storage or networking service.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe Microsoft Entra ID

distractors.C: Physical datacenter security is always Microsoft's responsibility, never the customer's.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the shared responsibility model

questions.stem: A customer running Azure virtual machines asks who secures the physical servers and the datacenter they sit in. Who holds that responsibility?

options.text: The customer, because they deployed the VMs
Whichever party is named in an Azure Policy
It is split evenly between the two parties
Microsoft, in every cloud service type

distractors.B: Azure Policy governs how resources are configured, not who owns the physical datacenter.
distractors.C: The physical datacenter is not a shared or split responsibility; it is entirely the provider's.

explanation.exam_pattern: Physical hosts, physical network, and the datacenter are always the provider's.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the shared responsibility model

questions.stem: As an organization moves the same workload from IaaS toward SaaS, how does the division of responsibilities change?

options.text: The customer manages more and the provider manages less
Responsibilities stay identical across all service types
The customer becomes responsible for the physical datacenter
The customer manages less and the provider manages more

explanation.correct: Moving from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, the provider takes on more (such as the OS and applications) and the customer retains less, ending at data, devices, and identities.

distractors.A: This is reversed; responsibility shifts toward the provider as you move toward SaaS.
distractors.B: The responsibility split is exactly what changes across service types.
distractors.C: The physical datacenter is never the customer's responsibility in any service type.

explanation.exam_pattern: More managed service (toward SaaS) means less customer responsibility.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the shared responsibility model

questions.stem: A provider owns the hardware and offers services over the internet to many organizations that share it. Which cloud model is this?

explanation.correct: A public cloud is owned by a third-party provider, shared across many customers (multi-tenant), and delivered over the internet with no up-front hardware cost.

distractors.A: A hybrid cloud combines public and private environments; this describes only the public part.
distractors.B: A private cloud's resources are used exclusively by a single organization, not shared.
distractors.D: An on-premises datacenter is owned and operated by the organization itself, not a provider.

explanation.exam_pattern: Shared, provider-owned, internet-delivered, multi-tenant = public cloud.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe cloud computing - public, private, and hybrid cloud models

questions.stem: A bank wants cloud-style resources used exclusively by itself, with the greatest control over the environment. Which deployment model fits best?

explanation.correct: A private cloud dedicates resources to a single organization (hosted on-site or by a third party), giving the most control over the environment.

distractors.B: A public cloud is shared and multi-tenant, offering less control over the stack.
distractors.C: A hybrid cloud mixes private and public; the scenario asks only for exclusive use.
distractors.D: Multi-tenant SaaS shares infrastructure among customers, the opposite of exclusive use.

explanation.exam_pattern: Used by a single organization with maximum control = private cloud.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe cloud computing - public, private, and hybrid cloud models

questions.stem: A retailer keeps sensitive records in its own datacenter but shifts extra holiday traffic to Azure when demand spikes. Which model is this?

explanation.correct: A hybrid cloud combines a private (on-premises) environment with the public cloud, letting workloads move between them, such as bursting to Azure for peak demand.

distractors.A: A private cloud alone cannot burst into Azure's public capacity for the spike.
distractors.C: Multicloud means using more than one public provider; here on-premises is combined with one cloud.
distractors.D: A public-cloud-only approach would not keep the records in the company's own datacenter.

explanation.exam_pattern: On-premises plus public cloud working together = hybrid.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe cloud computing - public, private, and hybrid cloud models

questions.stem: A team provisions Azure resources and is billed only for the compute and storage it actually uses, with no up-front purchase. What is this called?

explanation.correct: The consumption-based model means you pay only for the resources you use, with no up-front cost, and your spend scales up or down with usage.

distractors.B: A fixed annual license charges a set fee regardless of how much you use.
distractors.C: A perpetual license is a one-time purchase to own software, not pay-per-use.
distractors.D: Capital expenditure is up-front spending on owned infrastructure, not usage-based billing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Pay only for what you use, no up-front cost = consumption-based model.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the consumption-based model

questions.stem: Moving from buying its own servers to paying monthly for Azure services changes how a company accounts for IT spend. Which shift occurs?

options.text: From capital expenditure (CapEx) to operational expenditure (OpEx)
From operational expenditure (OpEx) to capital expenditure (CapEx)
From a subscription model to an up-front purchase
From a variable cost to a one-time fixed cost

explanation.correct: Buying servers is CapEx (up-front investment in owned assets); paying for cloud services as you use them is OpEx, so the cloud shifts spending from CapEx to OpEx.

distractors.B: This reverses the direction; cloud moves spend toward OpEx, not CapEx.
distractors.C: Pay-as-you-go cloud is the opposite of an up-front purchase.
distractors.D: Cloud billing is an ongoing variable cost, not a one-time fixed cost.

explanation.exam_pattern: Cloud pay-as-you-go turns big up-front CapEx into ongoing OpEx.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Compare cloud pricing (CapEx vs OpEx)

questions.stem: A finance manager records a large one-time purchase of on-premises servers and datacenter equipment. How is this expense best classified?

explanation.correct: A one-time, up-front purchase of physical infrastructure that is owned and depreciated over time is a capital expenditure (CapEx).

distractors.A: OpEx is ongoing pay-for-use spending, not an up-front hardware purchase.
distractors.C: Consumption-based spending is billed by actual usage, unlike a fixed hardware buy.
distractors.D: Pay-as-you-go describes cloud billing tied to usage, not owning hardware up front.

explanation.exam_pattern: Up-front, owned, depreciated hardware = CapEx; ongoing usage billing = OpEx.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Compare cloud pricing (CapEx vs OpEx)

questions.stem: An insurer must keep one legacy app on-premises for compliance while gradually moving other systems to Azure. Which model supports this?

explanation.correct: Hybrid lets the insurer keep some workloads on-premises (for compliance) while using the public cloud for others, which also eases a gradual migration.

distractors.A: A public-cloud-only model cannot keep the legacy app running on-premises.
distractors.B: A private-cloud-only model would not use Azure's public cloud for the other systems.
distractors.D: The consumption-based model is a pricing approach, not a deployment model.

explanation.exam_pattern: Keep some on-prem, use cloud for the rest, migrate over time = hybrid.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe cloud computing - public, private, and hybrid cloud models

questions.stem: A customer reviews the shared responsibility model across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Which TWO responsibilities always remain the customer's? (Choose two.)

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the shared responsibility model

questions.stem: Compared with running its own private cloud, what key advantage does an organization gain by using the public cloud?

options.text: Exclusive, single-tenant use of all physical servers
No capital expense for hardware, since the provider owns and maintains it
Elimination of all of its security responsibilities
Full physical control of the datacenter

explanation.exam_pattern: Public cloud = no hardware CapEx, provider-owned; beware 'eliminate all security' absolutes.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe cloud computing - public, private, and hybrid cloud models

questions.stem: A company wants its customer-facing app to stay up with as little downtime as possible. Which cloud benefit most directly addresses this goal?

explanation.correct: High availability keeps applications running with minimal downtime, typically backed by service-level agreements and redundant infrastructure.

distractors.A: Economies of scale is about lower unit cost from aggregated demand, not uptime.
distractors.C: Capital expenditure is a spending type, not an availability benefit.
distractors.D: Governance is about meeting standards and compliance, not keeping an app online.

explanation.exam_pattern: Minimize downtime / keep apps running = high availability.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability

questions.stem: To handle a heavier database, an admin raises an existing Azure VM's CPU and memory instead of adding more VMs. What is this?

explanation.correct: Vertical scaling (scaling up or down) changes the power - CPU, memory - of an existing resource rather than adding more instances.

distractors.A: Geo-replication copies data across regions; it is not a form of scaling a VM's size.
distractors.B: Horizontal scaling adds or removes separate instances, which the admin did not do.
distractors.C: Load balancing distributes traffic across instances; it does not resize a VM.

explanation.exam_pattern: Bigger/stronger single resource = vertical (up); more instances = horizontal (out).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability

questions.stem: As web traffic grows, a team adds more identical VM instances behind a load balancer instead of resizing one server. Which scaling is this?

explanation.correct: Horizontal scaling (scaling out or in) adds or removes instances to meet demand, exactly what adding more VMs behind a load balancer does.

distractors.A: Vertical scaling resizes a single resource, which the team specifically avoided.
distractors.B: Failover switches to a standby after a fault; it does not add capacity for growth.
distractors.D: 'Capital scaling' is not a real scaling type.

explanation.exam_pattern: Add or remove instances = horizontal (out/in).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability

questions.stem: A workload automatically gains resources during busy hours and releases them when demand drops, with no manual action. Which capability is this?

explanation.correct: Elasticity is the ability to automatically add resources as demand rises and remove them as it falls, so capacity matches load.

distractors.A: Fault tolerance is surviving component failure, not matching capacity to demand.
distractors.C: High availability is about uptime, not automatically right-sizing capacity.
distractors.D: Capital expenditure is a spending type, not a scaling behavior.

explanation.exam_pattern: Automatic scale-out under load and scale-in when idle = elasticity.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability

questions.stem: A design goal is for the system to recover from failures and keep functioning, partly by deploying across multiple regions. Which benefit is this?

explanation.correct: Reliability is a system's ability to recover from failures and continue to function; the cloud's distributed, multi-region design supports it.

distractors.A: Consumption-based pricing is a cost model, not a resilience property.
distractors.B: Manageability is about operating and managing resources, not recovering from failure.
distractors.D: Vertical scaling resizes a resource; it is not itself a recover-from-failure goal.

explanation.exam_pattern: Recover from failure and keep running = reliability (a Well-Architected pillar).

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability

questions.stem: An architect uses autoscaling and load balancing so the application's performance can be forecast as demand changes. Which cloud benefit does this support?

explanation.correct: Performance predictability means forecasting the resources needed for a good experience; autoscaling, load balancing, and high availability support it.

distractors.A: Capital expenditure is a spending model, not a performance benefit.
distractors.B: Multi-tenancy describes shared infrastructure, not performance forecasting.
distractors.C: Governance concerns compliance and standards, not forecasting performance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Forecast performance via autoscale/load balancing/HA = performance predictability.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability

questions.stem: A finance team wants to forecast and track Azure spending using the pricing calculator and cost-management tools. Which cloud benefit is this?

explanation.correct: Cost predictability means forecasting and tracking spend; tools such as the Pricing Calculator, TCO Calculator, and Microsoft Cost Management support it.

distractors.A: Private-cloud isolation is a deployment trait, not a cost-forecasting benefit.
distractors.C: High availability is about uptime, not forecasting cost.
distractors.D: Horizontal scaling is about capacity, not predicting spend.

explanation.exam_pattern: Forecast/track spend with calculators and cost management = cost predictability.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability

questions.stem: By choosing managed Azure services, a team lets the provider handle operating-system patching while it still sets access controls. Which benefit is this?

options.text: The security benefits of the cloud

explanation.correct: The cloud lets you choose your level of responsibility: with managed (PaaS/SaaS) services the provider patches the OS, strengthening security while you manage access.

distractors.B: Economies of scale is about lower price from aggregated demand, not security.
distractors.C: Vertical scaling is about capacity, not who patches the operating system.
distractors.D: Consumption-based billing is a cost model, not a security benefit.

explanation.exam_pattern: Provider handles patching in managed services = a cloud security benefit.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of security and governance

questions.stem: A company must ensure every deployed resource follows corporate standards, using policies and templates that flag anything non-compliant. Which cloud benefit is this?

explanation.correct: Governance uses tools such as Azure Policy, resource locks, and templates to enforce corporate and regulatory standards and flag non-compliant resources.

distractors.A: High availability is about uptime, not compliance with corporate standards.
distractors.B: Elasticity is automatic scaling with demand, not enforcing standards.
distractors.C: Capital expenditure is a spending type, unrelated to enforcing standards.

explanation.exam_pattern: Enforce standards/compliance via policy and templates = governance.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of security and governance

questions.stem: An operations team sets resources to scale automatically, deploys from reusable templates, and gets health alerts. Which kind of management is this?

distractors.B: Management IN the cloud is about the tools used to interact with Azure, not these tasks.
distractors.C: Identity governance is a narrower security/access topic, not this set of operational tasks.
distractors.D: On-premises management is not cloud management at all.

explanation.exam_pattern: Autoscale, templates, monitoring/alerts = management OF the cloud.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud

questions.stem: An administrator interacts with Azure through the web portal, the CLI, PowerShell, and REST APIs. Which type of manageability does this describe?

explanation.correct: Management IN the cloud is how you interact with your environment: the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, and APIs.

distractors.A: 'Capital expenditure management' is a spending concept, not a way to interact with Azure.
distractors.B: Management OF the cloud is automating, scaling, and monitoring the resources themselves.
distractors.C: Horizontal scaling is a scaling method, not a management interface.

explanation.exam_pattern: Portal, CLI, PowerShell, APIs = management IN the cloud.

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud

questions.stem: An app's load swings sharply through the day and the team wants Azure to match capacity to demand. Which TWO scaling approaches apply? (Choose two.)

Switch the billing from OpEx to CapEx
Add or remove VM instances (horizontal scaling)

references: Microsoft Learn (AZ-900): Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability

questions.stem: A team wants cloud servers where it controls the operating system and installed software while the provider runs the physical hardware. Which service type?
